corpusSource: Page classes and domains selected from the Web Bench READ subset (github.com/Halluminate/WebBench, MIT, webbenchfinal.csv: 1637 READ tasks over 448 domains; stackexchange/stackoverflow/github are among its top domains). Web Bench itself is a LIVE agent-task set with no frozen HTML and no goldens, so it cannot be the blocking gate directly — it is the corpus SELECTOR. Snapshots here are frozen at capture time and are never re-fetched by the gate; live targets and the Firecrawl side-by-side belong to the cron/dispatch half of the D6 hybrid gate.

assertions.why: A section heading deep in the body: proves extraction reached past the lead, not just the intro.
The canonical worked example. Short alphanumeric strings are the first thing an over-aggressive boilerplate stripper eats.
Section structure must survive. Zero means the document flattened; a huge count means nav lists were mistaken for headings.
Truncation caps scored 5.33 on the July bench — a hard lower bound is the cheapest detector for a silently-truncated body.
The alphabet and worked-example tables are the page's substance; a flattened table loses the rows but keeps the prose, so char count alone would not notice.
Structured mode must see the same tables the markdown does.
Definition lists are a distinct extraction path from tables and regress independently.
Wikipedia ships JSON-LD; losing it means the jsonld path broke, not that the page changed.
A real header cell — proves headers are parsed, not merged into the first data row.
MediaWiki skip-link. The single most common Wikipedia boilerplate leak.
Footer chrome.
Header account chrome.
Infobox label. Infoboxes are markup-dense and are what naive extractors drop first.
An infobox VALUE, not just its label — proves the label/value pairing survived.
Long-article lower bound; the upper bound catches nav/footer bloat being counted as content.
This page carries the chunk-layout and colour-type tables that make it a table fixture.
21 at capture; a large drop means the table detector regressed, not that Wikipedia changed (the snapshot is frozen).
A header from the PNG chunk-layout table — the page's most structurally load-bearing table.
MediaWiki skip-link.
MediaWiki footer marker.
Page title in body — a site-specific extractor that mis-selects the root node loses this.
A mid-document definition term; proves the long definition list was not truncated.
The LAST class of the list — the strongest single truncation detector on this page.
Truncation bound for the docs class.
82 at capture. This page is definition-lists rather than tables, which is a separate structured path from the Wikipedia fixtures and would otherwise be untested.
MDN skip-link.

assertions.why: The README's own description — the GitHub site extractor exists to return README content rather than page chrome.
Below this the extractor returned the file listing without the README.
A README without code blocks means fenced code was flattened into prose — the highest-value loss on a developer page.
The file listing is a real table; 6 at capture.
A file-listing row — proves the repo tree table parsed into cells rather than one blob.

assertions.value: You signed out in another tab
assertions.why: GitHub's session-chrome string; a classic leak from the app shell.

fixtures.licence: Cloudflare interstitial served to a plain HTTP client; no site content captured

assertions.why: A challenge shell must never be returned as a substantial page. This fixture exists because the corpus needs the failure case, not only pages that work — the snapshot is what stackoverflow.com actually served a plain HTTP client at capture time.
Pins what the extractor currently DOES return, so a change in that behaviour shows up as a diff instead of passing silently.

assertions.value: Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue
assertions.why: KNOWN GAP, expected to fail at baseline: challenge chrome is still returned as content at the extractor layer. The classification that catches this lives downstream in the fetch pipeline, not here. Recorded as a failing baseline assertion so it is visible and measured rather than assumed fixed.
A challenge shell has no tables; a non-zero count would mean the detector is hallucinating structure out of markup.
